references.text: The Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in the mountains came down and struck the Israelites, driving them back all the way to Horma. This is the early mention of Horma in connection with Israel's defeat.
The Canaanite king of Arad attacked Israel, and Israel made a vow to the Lord to devote their cities to destruction. The place was called Horma, which means 'destruction'.
Judah and Simeon struck down the Canaanites who lived in Zephath and completely destroyed the city. The city was called Horma, confirming the conquest mentioned in Joshua 12:14.
David sent some of the plunder to the elders in Horma, showing that the city was part of Judah's territory and had a connection with David's supporters.
